items_missed: Never asked 'How are you today?' — jumped straight from greeting into the date-change request.
No agenda statement ('I'll gather some details, then walk you through pricing, takes about 10-15 minutes, sound good?') before starting the probe.
Never asked whether the customer needs packing services.
Never asked the open-ended stressor question (e.g. 'anything you're particularly worried about with this move?').
No 'pricing is super simple' opener before launching into the hourly rate.
Did not explicitly list what's included in the rate (gas, truck, wrap pads, bands, tools) — went straight to rate/trip fee/overnight fee.
No sense-check ('does that make sense?') after explaining the 2.5-hour minimum and 15-minute proration.
Save Your Ass speech was generic ('consolidate items into boxes') with no specific examples (toys, garden tools, drawer contents, wall photos) and no closing 'does that make sense?'.
Estimate walkthrough had no equivalents (e.g. school-bus reference) and did not cite traffic as a driving variable, only truck weight/highway speed.
Never attempted to book/lock the date on the call — confirmed 7/24 availability but ended with 'whatever you decide you can just give us a call or text back' instead of asking to schedule now.
Never used the customer's name ('Brock') once in the entire 22-minute call — addressed him only as 'sir.'
Insurance explanation covered the $2,000 No Worries cap but omitted the 60-cent/lb baseline liability standard.
No humor or rapport-building moment; call stayed strictly transactional throughout.
top_strength: Cameron thoroughly probed the move specifics (storage unit dimensions, floor/door access, distances, inventory) and gave Brock a fully itemized, transparent breakdown of how the 9-hour/$3,258 estimate was built.
coaching_note: Cameron never used Brock's name and never asked for a same-call booking commitment despite confirming 7/24 availability — practice closing every re-quote/update call with an explicit ask like 'want me to go ahead and lock in Friday the 24th right now?' and use the customer's first name at least a few times to build rapport.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and functional with a few soft affirmations ('perfect,' 'got it,' 'have a wonderful day') but no use of the customer's name and no acknowledgment of moving-related stress, keeping the call transactional throughout.
audio_review_reason: Several transcript lines are garbled or cut off mid-sentence (e.g. 'is it, is it near the for the doors are?', 'the floor is located on'), which limits confidence in judging Cameron's actual vocal tone from text alone.
